claims.claim: Prediction state may miss a secondary target/responsibility.
Utility/loss-defined decision states over predictive/causal states and entropy/complexity of such decision states.
For a responsibility whose Bayes-optimal action is not measurable from the linguistic predictive state, minimum exact ANY_OPTIMAL_ACTION state cost beyond S_P is min_d H(d(H)|S_P).
If some Bayes-optimal responsibility policy is a function of S_P, then static extra cost is zero; this includes Brodu-like decisions determined entirely from the same future distribution.
Positive static responsibility cost occurs iff no Bayes-optimal policy is implementable from S_P alone.
Entropy-minimal exact predictive state is isomorphic to S_P on support.
Static responsibility state is minimum-entropy predictive-refining action-compatible partition, equivalent to optimal selector entropy.
Dynamic responsibility state is minimum-entropy predictive-refining action-compatible right-congruent partition.
Dynamic optimum equals minimum over Bayes-optimal selectors of coarsest right-congruent refinement cost.
Dynamic epistemic optionality premium Omega_dyn=C_dyn^*-C_stat^* quantifies state needed solely for future responsibility update after optimizing current Bayes policy.
Canonical provenance process has C_stat^*=0, C_dyn^*=1 bit, Omega_dyn=1 bit.
Exact state regimes P0 predictive-decisional, P1 static cross-channel refinement, P2 prospective refinement are classified by C0^* and Omega_dyn.
Minimum k-horizon state costs C_k^* and premiums Omega_k are monotone and stabilize in finite systems; K_epi records the stabilization horizon.
Responsibility-family overhead bounded by non-predictive history; separating families force full-history retention within predictive fibres.
Matched linguistic prediction and current responsibility performance do not certify prospective revision adequacy; a controlled future-evidence test is a distinct representation audit.
